title: Signal onboarding quickstart + widget templates
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, copy-and-paste friendly quickstart for bringing a new observability signal (metric or trace span) into Redwood's public metric catalog and into a minimal dashboard. Goal: cut friction for engineers so new metrics are shippable with ownership, alerting guidance, and a displayable widget set.

Summary (one-liner): make it trivial to add a metric + 3 small widgets + a trace link so feature owners have usable visibility within one PR.

Quick onboarding checklist (minimal viable signal):
- 1) Create metric in runtime code (counter/gauge/histogram) with stable name and labels.
- 2) Add metric metadata file (yaml/json entry in /observability/metrics-catalog) with owner, description, unit, SLI mapping, suggested alert thresholds.
- 3) Add a minimal Grafana panel JSON (see widget templates below) or a PromQL snippet for each of the three canonical widgets.
- 4) Add span instrumentation for the same code path (span name + important attrs).
- 5) Open one PR that includes runtime change, metadata, and dashboard snippets; assign to eng-observability for review.
- 6) After merge, verify metric ingestion for 24 hours and confirm the dashboard renders. If the metric is high-cardinality, add a sampling plan or cardinality cap in the metadata.

Metric naming and metadata guidelines (short):
- Naming: <product>_<component>_<what>_<unit_opt>. Use snake_case. Example: inference_server_request_count_total, model_kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- Types: suffix counters with _total, histograms with _bucket/_sum/_count (Prometheus conventions), gauges with units when appropriate (_concurrent_sessions).
- Labels: keep small and well-defined. Typical labels: model, model_version, route, customer_tier, region, error_code. Avoid free-form ids.
- Metadata fields required: owner (email), short_description, long_description, unit, type, suggested_sli (yes/no), suggested_alert (threshold + rationale), cardinality_risk (low/medium/high), deprecation_date (optional).

Suggested metric definitions (examples):
- inference_request_total (counter)
  - description: total number of inference requests received by route
  - labels: model, route, region, status_code
  - useful PromQL (rps): sum(rate(inference_request_total[1m])) by (route)
  - dashboard widget type: single-stat + small sparklines for top routes

- inference_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - description: request latency including queueing and execution
  - labels: model, route, batch_size
  - useful PromQL (p95 by model): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
  - widget type: time-series (p50/p95/p99), heatmap by model + seq_len if available

- kv_cache_hit_total (counter)
  - description: number of KV cache hits at runtime
  - labels: model, route
  - derived metric: kv_cache_hit_ratio = sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[5m]))
  - widget type: gauge + time series of ratio

Tracing conventions (minimal):
- Span names: <service>.<operation> (e.g., inference_server.decode, inference_runtime.kv_lookup)
- Top-level request span should have attributes: model.name, model.version, route, request_id, trace_sampling_reason
- Instrument key sub-operations: tokenizer, kv_lookup, forward_pass, compile/kernels, postprocess.
- Important span tags to capture: batch_size, seq_len, kv_cache_hit (true/false), fallback_model (if used), node_id (for routing).
- Sampling strategy: adaptive front-line sampling + tail-sampling for errors. Practical rule: 0.1% baseline sample of successful requests, 100% of requests with error_code!=0, and 100% of traces flagged by anomaly detectors (latency spike or sudden error rate).
- Trace link on dashboard: add a panel with a direct query for traces where trace.tags.request_id = ${request_id} or trace.tag.route = 'X'.

Widget templates (copy-paste):
- Widget A: "Topline KPIs" (row 1)
  - panels: RPS (sum(rate(inference_request_total[1m]))), p95 latency (histogram_quantile(0.95,...)), error rate (sum(rate(inference_errors_total[5m]))/sum(rate(inference_request_total[5m])))
  - layout guidance: small single-stat panels with delta and sparkline; one per KPI; color thresholds: green/yellow/red per SLO

- Widget B: "Per-model performance"
  - panels: time series p50/p95 by model (use Grafana split series), table of top 10 models by request volume, heatmap of latency by seq_len if available
  - query examples: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))

- Widget C: "Failure traces and sample"
  - panels: list of top error codes (by rate), direct link to Jaeger/Tempo query prefilling trace_id when present, sample traces panel (tail-sampled recent errors)

- Widget D: "Cost & Efficiency" (optional)
  - panels: tokens_emitted_total per route, token_cost_estimate (derived metric), avg_batch_size histogram. Useful for Optimize team recommendations.

Dashboard layout recommendation (small feature-level dashboard):
- Row 0: metadata header (owner, oncall, last updated, metric tags)
- Row 1: Topline KPIs (Widget A)
- Row 2: Per-model performance + heatmap (Widget B)
- Row 3: Failures + trace links (Widget C)
- Row 4: Cost/Efficiency (Widget D) + notes/todo

Ownership and lifecycle (practical steps):
- Metric PR must include: code, tests (if applicable), metadata entry, and three Grafana panel JSON snippets. Reviewer: eng-observability.
- After merge: assign a 1-week observation window. If metric shows high-cardinality or causes billing spike, engage infra and product to remediate.
- Deprecation: set deprecation_date in metadata; create a cleanup ticket; maintain shim metrics for 30 days with a clear migration plan.

Cardinality checklist (short):
- Is there any label that can be arbitrarily large (customer id, full prompt hash)? If yes -> block and propose bucketing or hashing to fixed buckets.
- Use label value whitelists where possible (region, tier).
- If high-cardinality is unavoidable, mark cardinality_risk = high and propose sampling strategy.

Review heuristics for eng-observability (notes to reviewer):
- Verify metric semantics against code (counter vs gauge).
- Validate label set and check for free-text labels.
- Confirm that trace attributes expose the routing choices needed for debugging.
- Check that the dashboard panels are useful on first glance (no 5000-line legend).

Example "ready" PR checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Runtime instrumentation added and unit-tested
- [ ] Metric metadata entry added (owner, desc, unit, cardinality)
- [ ] 3 dashboard panels added (topline, per-model, errors)
- [ ] Trace spans instrumented for key operations
- [ ] Eng-observability reviewer assigned

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we compress model.version label space for nightly canaries vs stable models? (proposal: model_channel label: stable/canary/nightly)
- We still need an agreed-upon JSON schema for metric metadata in repo (blocking: OBS-4321).
- Should we auto-generate Grafana panels from metadata for common patterns? (low effort, high ROI)

References and quick links:
- Signal onboarding confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Signal+Onboarding
- Jira: OBS-4321 (metric metadata schema)
- PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/128

Notes to self / shorthand (informal):
- Keep the initial widget set tiny. Engineers ignore dashboards with 40 panels.
- Aim for 3 actionable things per dashboard: detect, drill, debug.
- Encourage metric owners to add a 1-paragraph playbook in metadata for common runbook steps.
